title: Remarkable Woman
paragraphs: "Somehow... it feels like one of those monsters you hunt in video games... even though it walks on two legs."
"It’d be fun to peel off that snowy armor one piece at a time."
"Yeah, there’s something satisfying about destroying its body parts, isn’t there?"
"My heroes... that might sound a bit indecent."
“Just hearing it like that, yeah, it does.”

As we were having this carefree exchange, the panda shrugged his shoulders with a “here we go again” look and let out a sigh. By the way, both Kou and Yuki-chan were silently watching how things unfolded.
“Let’s go, you lot! Smash this fool’s ice statue!”
The old mammoth, clearly annoyed that none of us—including Father—showed the slightest sign of panic, gave the order.
“‘‘‘Alright!’’’”

Six mammoths marched toward the elephant, who was swirling like a blizzard tornado. Thud, thud—their footsteps are unnecessarily loud. But is the elephant inside the whirlwind really turned into an ice statue?
“The Queen of Earthquakes, the very source of power, commands: Unravel the truth once more, and strike those men with a blow of earth that pierces right through them!”
“Drifa Earth Spike!”
As an exceptionally loud rumble echoed through the air, the ground formed a Continental Cleft, and pillars of earth shot out toward the surrounding mammoths.
“What—Gaaaaaaaaaaah!?”
“Gyaaaaaaa—”
“No way—it can’t be—”

The pillars of earth struck every single one of them squarely in the solar plexus, sending them all flying into the air. With another deep rumble, the blizzard tornado was blown away in an instant, revealing an elephant covered in a light dusting of snow.
“I used to look up to it back in the day. But once you’ve seen the world, you realize whether or not you can use ice and snow Magic is completely irrelevant. Lady Rainy was right after all.”
With a THUD, the mammoths were slammed into the ground.
“Guuuuuuu…”
“Ugh…”
“Kuuuuu…”

It seems the mammoths, due to their massive size, aren’t used to knowing how to break their fall when they’re slammed into the ground. Elephants, on the other hand… even when they were deftly tossed aside by the panda’s grandfather and grandmother, they still managed to break their fall, so it’s clear they’re technically superior.
“Come on, it wouldn’t be any fun if it ended right here, would it? Get back on your feet already.”
The elephant gives the mammoths a sharp beckoning gesture.
“You bastard… Don’t underestimate meeeee!”

It’s not the old mammoth, but what appears to be the elephant’s older brother who charges at the elephant wielding a hammer. …His movements are slower than the elephant’s. It would be impressive if it landed, but an attack that misses is meaningless.
“Hmph!”
The elephant stomps his right foot hard toward his opponent.
“Whoa!?”
A massive shockwave ripples through the charging mammoth’s legs, causing him to rise slightly off the ground. Seizing the moment, the elephant slams a shoulder tackle right into the mammoth’s gut.
“Ugh—”
The mammoth took the tackle perfectly and was sent flying through the air. Thud! One mammoth is knocked out.
“Oh my, was that too much for the young master? Hahahahaha, what a joke. “Come on, come at me!”
The elephant is taunting the other mammoths, who are standing there dumbfounded at the sight of their fallen comrade.
“H-haaaaaaaaaaaah!”

Oh? Three mammoths are charging in, swinging the iron balls strapped to their waists. And it looks like they’re even using their sharp tusks to stab. As expected, they rely on sheer volume of attacks.
“It’s kind of like a heavy tank, isn’t it? And since they’re even using ice magic, I can see why they’re considered strong.”
“That’s true… but—”
“Oryaaaaa!”
The elephant countered the three mammoths’ charge by hurling rocks he’d pulled from the ground, then grabbed one mammoth by the tusk and slammed it hard into the others.
“Guaaaaaaaah!”
“Kyaaaaaa!?”
“Ughhhhhh!?”
The three mammoths were rolled into a ball and sent tumbling. Facing the mammoths that were still trying to get back on their feet, Zou wore an air of authority.
“It seems that alone won’t be enough to get through to Lord Elmero.”
It certainly looks that way. For that elephant, those guys are a piece of cake. After all, he’s a fine elephant.
“Elephant, gooooooo!”
Father looks a little flustered by my cheering. It’s probably because I suddenly yelled right next to him.
“Come on, come on, come on! How long are you going to stay crawling on the ground? Oh, do you like kissing the ground? Well, I’ll show you then!”
The mammoths, who had been thrown aside and were trying to get back up, are now forced back down as vines of dirt shoot up from the ground and pin them to the earth.
“Guh… This is nothing… Guh…”
The bound mammoths try to break free from their restraints, but they can’t budge at all. An elephant approaches one of them, lifts a foot, and lightly stomps on the mammoth’s head.
“There you go—this is what you like, isn’t it, you pervert?”

“ As a reward… I’ve actually been kicked before!
“Shield Hero, do you get it now? That’s Zeltoble—the spectacle Elmero used to put on.”
“Ah… yeah. She really is the Queen, isn’t she?”

That’s certainly true. I know that too. I suppose it’s just one of those quirks—or maybe it’s part of her act. Even my past self—a pig who’d never known romance—had seen a pig that strange before. Anyway, the mammoth being trampled by the elephant is desperately trying to break free from its restraints; it looks like it’s trying some underhanded tactics, like sweeping with its trunk.
“Oh my, what a nasty habit that trunk has.”
With a thud, the elephant stomped down hard on the mammoth’s trunk.
“Gugyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!?”
“Oh, for heaven’s sake. You’re so noisy!”
The moment the elephant stopped stomping and stomped its foot down on the ground, a shockwave seemed to rip through the restrained mammoth’s abdomen.
That alone seemed to be enough to make the three mammoths foam at the mouth and pass out.
“Petty. Who was it again? The one who said something about ‘one man against a thousand’… or that Zeltoble was a lowly country? Is this all you’ve got?”
Saying this, Zou made a taunting beckoning gesture toward the old mammoth responsible. Hmm, he’s in top form.
“Guh…”
“This is exactly what they mean by a blockhead. How does it feel? How does it feel to be completely outclassed by the thorn in your side you’ve been mocking all this time?”
"Don't get too cocky, aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!"
The old mammoth hurls a hammer at him. The elephant deftly catches the hammer with his trunk, spins around once, and throws it right back.
“What!?”
Thud! It hit right between the eyes of the mammoth standing next to the old one… who appeared to be its mother.
“Agh!?”
It seems it hit just the right spot. The mammoth—presumably the mother—rolled her eyes back and collapsed with a thud.
“Oh, right. I might as well get back at you for your hysterics.”

So, the elephant stomped its feet again. A column of dirt shot up from the ground, pummeling the mammoth—who appeared to be the mother—in the face, and the hammer, flung upward by the impact, rained down on its tusks as if to deliver the finishing blow, snapping one clean off.
“There, all done. I can’t wait to hear what kind of scream she’ll let out when she regains consciousness.”
How should I put it… it’s a truly brutal family feud. If the mammoth family and the elephant were human, it would make for quite a spectacular scene. Neither of them shows any mercy.
“Eek…”
The remaining mammoths—other than the old one—let out cries of fear.

The elephant approached the cowering mammoths, step by step, with a thud, thud, thud. Eventually… as the elephant came right up in front of them, the terrified mammoth lost all its nerve and collapsed onto the ground.
“It seems the battles of the Puhant family are rather tame, don’t they? This… is what the real world is like!”
“Gua—”

Then, the elephant pulled a rock from the ground and hurled it at the cowering mammoth. With a thud, the frightened mammoth was pinned beneath the rock and knocked out. By the way, it doesn’t seem to be dead.
“Well then, as for the rest…”
Zou turned his gaze toward the remaining old mammoth.
“Grandpa, come on, go ahead and try to snap my trunk.”
“Grrrr… Do you really think you’ll get away with this?!”

“If I didn’t think so, I wouldn’t be doing this, would I? Besides, I’ve already been banished from this household. I couldn’t care less if a family of complete strangers holds a grudge against me. After all, this is Siltvelt—a country where one demonstrates one’s will through strength.”
Zou goes on at length about Siltvelt’s way of doing things.
“I competed against you all fair and square and won through strength. Despite that, trying to wield power like this… that’s just laughable. I wonder what the other nobles will think?”

Indeed, in Siltvelt—a land that values blood and strength—doing something so underhanded would surely invite ridicule. Of course, they might be pulling underhanded tricks behind the scenes, but if it ever came to light, it would be the end of them. In this regard, I feel that Siltvelt is stronger than Melromarc or Faubrey.
“Come on, show me that strength from the Great War you’ve been going on and on about until I’m sick of hearing it.”
“I don’t need to be told to show it! And I’m going to break your fangs! Dieeeeeeeeeeeeeee!”

The old mammoth, clutching the hammer that had been thrown back at him, brought it down toward the elephant. The elephant caught the hammer with one hand, then in one fluid motion slammed his fist into the mammoth’s belly, slammed the mammoth’s head—now bent into a “C” shape—against the ground with his trunk, and brought his free arm down on the mammoth’s remaining tusk.
“Pathetic. Just all talk, as expected.”
“Aaaaaaargh!?”

With a loud crack, the old mammoth collapsed, its tusk snapped in two. It was quite a heavyweight, spectacular battle, wasn’t it? Since they’re apparently fighting while severely overloaded… it turns out these mammoths are nothing but all show. Well, by our standards, it was a battle where their movements seemed rather sluggish. Dealing with them isn’t that hard, is it?
“Hmph, is that all you’ve got?”
And with that, the elephant who’d defeated six mammoths lets out a victorious cry. Snapping back to his senses, the elephant looks over at Father… and returns to his usual, gentle self.
“Elmero, you’re sooo cool!”

Kou raises both hands and walks toward Zou. As if to break the silence, Father claps his hands. In unison, Panda and Éclair start clapping too. Yuki-chan is clapping as well. I’ll join in too. Just then, a whistling sound comes from the roof of the mansion.
“Ah, those guys are… wait a minute…”
“We did it! Elmero!”
Zou picks up Kou, who had leaped at him.
“I suppose so. I do think I might have gone a little overboard… but I feel refreshed now.”
Still holding Kou, the elephant made her way over to Father. Then she shot a sharp glare at the mammoths who hadn’t participated in the duel.
“This should be the end of the duel, right? Now, as promised, don’t get involved with me or Lady Rainy anymore.”

Yes, she said it with a menacing edge to her voice. My, my… that was a battle that truly brought the term “heroic woman” to life. It seems that the people Kou takes a liking to tend to be quite strong-willed. Big Sister and her friend also showed their resolve when it really mattered.
In other words, Kou is… a bed-wetting shota! I’ll keep that firmly in mind. He’s a bed-wetting shota!
“So, as for the compensation… once we’re ready to move, just the bare minimum will do. Elmero, once you’ve finished preparing the items and the people you want to bring along, come back.”
“Yes, Shield Hero… I’m truly grateful for your consideration in every single detail.”
“Don’t worry about it. I’m pretty much the one who caused this whole commotion anyway. In fact, it ended up being the reason for our estrangement—are you okay with that?”
“…Yes. I’ve shaken off my doubts. Please don’t let it bother you, and I look forward to your continued support.”

With that, Zou saluted as if to prove his loyalty to Siltvelt, received permission from Father, and began his preparations. The flustered Kebamammoth watched Zou, the Mammoth, and Father, but Father wasn’t even glancing in his direction.
“If you want to get close to me, you’ll have to show me some impressive military achievements or other feats worthy of me. To be honest, I’m not really into people like you. Well then.”
Whoa… Father sure said that very clearly. He looks quite the playboy, doesn’t he? The problem is that his opponent is a mammoth Beastman.

But… it’s true that the Shaggy Mammoth’s appearance reminds me of a Crimson Swine, which I find off-putting. I don’t sense the same level of evil as a Crimson Swine, but I could really feel his shallow mindset—the idea that a man should just be swept off his feet by a woman’s charm.
“Panda.”
“What is it?”
“Is that flashy mammoth actually a beauty? I’m not really getting it.”
“Hmm… Even from my perspective, she’s a bit off, but from a Beastman’s point of view, her face and figure are pretty good. There’s no doubt she’s a beauty.”
